chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Abdullah ibn Junadab, who said:

Abbad ibn Maymun asked a man, while I was present, who had made a vow upon himself to fast and wished to travel to Mecca. Abdullah ibn Junadab said: I heard the one who narrated it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he was asked about a man who made a vow upon himself to fast, and his intention to visit Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) coincided with it. He said: 'He goes out and does not fast on the journey, and when he returns, he makes up for that.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a person who has vowed to fast but needs to travel and visit the Imam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Abdullah ibn Junadab highlights the practical flexibility granted to travelers who have vowed to fast, prioritizing the spiritual merit of visiting the Imam (Ziyarat) over strict fasting during the journey. The ruling emphasizes that the obligation is not voided but deferred, requiring the individual to perform *qada* (make-up) upon return, reflecting the Shia juristic balance between ritual devotion and the ease (*rukhas*) afforded to travelers.
